text:
The Kings might be the unluckiest team in the West right now. Los Angeles has 12 points from 15 games; by the chances it has created and allowed, it deserved 16.6. Over its last five it took 58% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and went 2-3, including a 5-2 loss to Pittsburgh on Saturday in which it had 59% of the expected goals. Adrian Kempe's hat trick against San Jose, the one that moved him past Dustin Brown on the franchise list, is the only night lately when the finishing matched the work. Our playoff odds still have them at 39%. That number will move fast if pucks start going in.

Nashville is the opposite story. The Predators have won four straight and outscored teams 15-8 in that run, and the chances mostly back it up (55% of the expected goals in those games), even if their season-long five-on-five share is a modest 46%. Juuse Saros has been the floor: +6.3 goals saved above expected this season after -10.2 last year. Steven Stamkos has moved into the all-time top five in power-play goals (Yahoo Sports), Roman Josi is one point from 800 for his career, and Shane Wright, acquired from Seattle for Matthew Wood, has slotted in next to Filip Forsberg.

There's a subplot on the Kings' side too. Erik Haula faces the Predators for the first time since leaving them after 132 games, and Mats Zuccarello could return, now cleared from ESPN's injury report. Anton Forsberg (projected) starts for Los Angeles at -0.8 goals saved above expected, which is the matchup's soft spot on paper.

Our numbers lean Kings, 3.12 expected goals to 2.87. Artemi Panarin is 74% for a point and Kempe 38% to score. Our sleeper is Quinton Byfield: 50% for a point against a season pace of 43%, because his line creates 4.01 expected goals per 60 when he's out there. Both teams are rested, two days off apiece, so nobody gets to blame the legs.
headline: The Kings keep outplaying people and losing

hunch.text: Our hunch: Byfield scores. The Kings' chances have been running ahead of their goals for two weeks, and the player whose line makes the most of them is the one we'd expect to cash in first.
